high_level_description: Strictly non-photographic, wordless Kinngait stonecut illustration: an Inuit artist offers one selected drawing while an Inuit master printmaker accepts only that sheet, every person and object carved as flat black, teal and rust shapes on cream paper with broad negative space, no gradients, modeled depth, writing or arrows.

compositional_deconstruction.background: A broad unprinted cream field surrounds one central black table shape and four asymmetrical teal and rust edge forms. The entire composition occupies one shallow frontal plane with generous negative space, without architectural room, horizon, window, realistic floor, receding perspective, museum display, sales counter, institutional sign, syllabic writing, letter, numeral, edition mark, caption, arrow, interface, diagram, flag, ranking badge, ceremonial object, or stereotyped Arctic scenery.

elements.desc: Older Inuit graphic artist at the left side of the table, medium-brown skin, long straight black hair streaked gray, teal sweater, charcoal trousers, and dark shoes. Calm and attentive, she offers exactly one flat drawing with both hands while three other drawings remain rolled beside her; she carries no contract, seal, money, or commanding object.

Adult Inuit master printmaker at the right side at equal scale, medium-brown skin, short black hair, rust work shirt, dark teal apron, charcoal trousers, and black shoes. He reaches with both open hands to accept only the offered sheet and looks directly at it; his stonecut tools remain local, with no restraint, order, badge, or compulsory mechanism.

Shared black worktable flattened into a broad asymmetrical shape with a cream upper surface and no receding edges. The selected drawing rests across its center between the artist’s and printmaker’s hands; one untouched stone block, an ink roller, a carving tool, and a wooden rubbing spoon remain grouped on the printmaker’s right side.

Single selected original drawing lying flat across the middle of the table, showing one black Arctic char curving around three rounded shoreline stones in bold uncomplicated contours. The cream sheet has generous blank margins and no signature, title, syllabic character, edition number, stamp, border, price, approval mark, or second image.

Shallow rust-colored tray beside the artist containing exactly three other drawings, each rolled separately and tied with plain cream cotton tape. Their image surfaces remain completely hidden, showing they have not been included in the accepted task; the tray bears no inventory label, selection rank, lock, seal, ownership mark, realistic depth, or decorative writing.
